directDependencies.name: tauri-plugin-dialog
directDependencies.selectionNote: 2.7.1 was published 2026-05-02 and supplies the official Rust blocking file-picker API on a worker thread. It is optional with the desktop-shell feature, and its JavaScript commands receive no WebView capability. 2.7.2 was published 2026-07-18 and remains inside the review window; its Android theming change is irrelevant to the first Windows proof.

directDependencies.name: zeroize
directDependencies.selectionNote: Current portable zeroization primitive used to clear Coredrill-owned secret strings and retrieved byte buffers before release; it does not claim control over copies owned by the WebView, operating system, or process environment.

directDependencies.name: zbus-secret-service-keyring-store
directDependencies.selectionNote: Current FreeDesktop Secret Service store, confined to Linux with default features disabled and the RustCrypto implementation selected. Coredrill serializes entry operations, fails closed when no unlocked Secret Service is available, and never falls back to plaintext storage.

directDependencies.name: apple-native-keyring-store
directDependencies.selectionNote: Current macOS login-Keychain store, target-confined with default features disabled and only the keychain implementation selected. Phase 0 does not request protected, biometric, access-group, or iCloud Keychain behavior; operations remain serialized and failures remain content-free.

directDependencies.name: windows-native-keyring-store
directDependencies.selectionNote: Current Windows Credential Manager store, target-confined with default features disabled so search and regex are absent. Coredrill serializes all entry operations because the upstream store warns that same-entry operations from different threads may not sequence reliably.

directDependencies.name: windows-sys
directDependencies.selectionNote: Current low-level Windows bindings, already present transitively and now declared directly with only Foundation/FileSystem features so Coredrill can call MoveFileExW with replace-existing and write-through flags for same-volume atomic recovery.

directDependencies.name: tauri
directDependencies.selectionNote: The Tauri test harness is confined to the Windows target that runs the platform application-data proof; portable no-default-feature Rust tests do not compile the Linux GTK shell graph.

advisoryReview.reviewNote: RustSec reports no vulnerability. The informational warnings are transitive Tauri/Wry cross-platform lock entries: GTK3/unic/proc-macro maintenance warnings plus glib 0.18.5 unsoundness. Windows and macOS do not compile the GTK3 path; Linux does, so its package remains diagnostic and release support cannot be accepted without an explicit NAT-008 decision that resolves or knowingly accepts the unsound graph.

licenseReview.note: License records and advisory dependency counts use different tool scopes and are not expected to match.

maintenanceWatch.reason: Two registry maintainers and a comparatively large Arborist subtree; review maintenance and replacement options before production dependency volume grows.

RustSec reports no vulnerability but records 14 unmaintained transitive warnings and glib 0.18.5 unsoundness in the Linux GTK3 path. The Phase 0 Linux AppImage is diagnostic only; public Linux desktop support remains blocked until the graph is replaced, remediated upstream, or accepted through an explicit risk decision.
TypeScript 7 adoption is blocked by the current typescript-eslint peer range and requires a mutually compatible release.
The runtime and type packages use release-age-reviewed versions while their current patch releases remain inside the 60-day window; re-evaluate them together after the newest type release ages out.
